chunks: Thus, they refused until war spread its wings and came to stay,
Its flames rose and became strong.
When the war had bitten us as well as them and pierced its talons into us as well as them,
they accepted what we had proposed to them.
So, we agreed to what they suggested and hastened to meet their request.
In this way, the plea became clear to them and no excuse was left to them.

key_terms.جَنَحَتِ الْحَرْبُ: war spread its wings and came to stay

ai.seo_question: What happened at Siffin when the war became costly for both sides?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) recounts how Muawiya’s forces delayed accepting arbitration until the mutual exhaustion of the Battle of Siffin made the stalemate unbearable, a strategic move to preserve their political legitimacy. This delay allowed Ali to establish the 'Hujjah' (clear proof) and remove any 'Ma'dhirah' (excuse) for their subsequent acceptance, highlighting the Shia view that the arbitration was a concession to necessity rather than a validation of Muawiya's claim. The passage underscores the principle that truth must be presented clearly before the opposing party can be held accountable for their rejection.
